candidates.source_title: Banned driver led police on high-speed chase through the streets of Rochdale
candidates.source_summary: Bilal Ishaq reached speeds more than three times the limit as he tried to outrun police motorcyclists in a black Mercedes
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A banned driver who led police on an 'extremely dangerous' chase through the streets of Rochdale has been jailed. Bilal Ishaq reached speeds more than three times the limit as he tried to outrun police motorcyclists in a black Mercedes. Police footage shows officers take up the pursuit on Foxholes Road after they suspected the 35-year-old of drug dealing. In the clip an officer can be heard saying 'It's a black Mercedes, believe he's drug dealing'. Ishaq can then be seen racing through residential streets at speeds of over 60mph. At one point he goes through a mini-roundabout on the wrong side of the road, narrowly avoiding a car pulling out from a side street. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter He also ran red lights and twice attempted to reverse into the police riders. As the pursuit comes to an end he pulls over and attempts to run away, as the abandoned Mercedes rolls down the street with the drivers door still open. Ishaq, of Hey Street, Rochdale, who was already serving two court-imposed driving bans following a separate dangerous driving offence in December 2025, was arrested shortly afterwards. He later admitted dangerous driving, driving whilst disqualified, failing to stop and driving without insurance and was jailed for 16 months and disqualified from driving for five years. Pc Matt Balkwell, from GMP's motorcycle unit, said: "This was an extremely dangerous piece of driving that put members of the public, officers and other road users at significant risk. Despite already being disqualified from driving, Ishaq chose to get behind the wheel and then attempted to evade police by driving recklessly through Rochdale at excessive speeds. To make sure you can see all of Manchester's court stories in your newsfeed - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source "His actions could easily have resulted in serious injury or loss of life. Thanks to the professionalism and determination of our officers involved, he was safely detained and has now been held accountable for his actions."

candidates.source_title: Cliff Byrne sets ambitious EFL Trophy aim for Doncaster Rovers
candidates.source_summary: Doncaster Rovers face Rochdale in the final group game of their EFL Trophy campaign
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Doncaster Rovers assistant coach Cliff Byrne believes Tuesday night’s EFL Trophy clash with Rochdale gives the players the perfect chance to try and rectify some of the problems that were apparent during last Saturday’s 6-1 defeat to MK Dons. Rovers go into their final group stage game in second position with a record of three points from their opening two matches. Grant McCann’s men were beaten 3-1 by Huddersfield Town in the first game before more recently recording a 1-0 win over Liverpool Under-21s. It means they are firmly on course to reach the knockout stages of the competition provided they can pick up all three points or either equal or better Liverpool Under-21’s result against Huddersfield. Rochdale are currently on one point. They drew 3-3 with Liverpool Under-21s before losing on penalties in the first match before falling to a disappointing 5-0 defeat against Huddersfield. Reflecting on the weekend, Byrne told club media: “It was a game that was important that we looked back over and looked through and it's a game we have to quickly learn from. “So our benefit now is we’ve got a game coming quickly, so we’re looking forward to that and to be able to go and put a performance on, it’s a game we need to win, it’s a cup competition and we want to progress to the next round, so that’s where the focus is.” Byrne continued: “I think when you come off a poor defeat and a poor performance couple with it, you definitely want an opportunity to go and rectify it and put it right, so when you have a game within a couple of days, that gives you the opportunity to go and do that and that’s exactly what we’ll be aiming to do.” Rovers reached the semi-final of this competition and only narrowly missed out on a first visit to Wembley since 2008 after losing to Stockport County in the semi-final. The South Yorkshire side have only ever won this competition once. That came in 2007 when Sean O’Driscoll’s men were triumphant over Bristol Rovers at the Millenium Stadium. “We want to go as far as we can,” said Byrne. “We made no bones about it last season and this season we have had some really good teams in our group, we’re down to the last game and it’s in our hands to progress to the next round.” The EFL Trophy is often seen as a competition for youngsters and squad players to get an opportunity. Byrne hinted that they’ll be some changes but also emphasized the importance of picking up a good result. He said: “It’s a game we want to win and the selection we have in mind is for that, to win the game and progress. “But there may be an opportunity for some players to get more minutes than they have in recent weeks but I think that's the nature of how the schedule is. It’s very hard to ask the same 11 to go time and time again. They’ll be opportunities in some areas but in others there won’t be.”

candidates.source_title: Watch as disqualified driver drives at three times speed limit in Rochdale chase
candidates.source_summary: Dramatic footage shows disqualified driver Bilal Ishaq speeding through Rochdale, running red lights and driving on the wrong side of the road during a police chase
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Dramatic footage has shown the moment a disqualified driver led police on a dangerous high-speed chase through Rochdale before crashing and trying to escape on foot. Bilal Ishaq, of Hey Street, Rochdale, drove at speeds more than three times the limit, went through red lights and travelled on the wrong side of the road as officers pursued him through the town. The 34-year-old also attempted to reverse into pursuing police vehicles on two occasions during the chase. The pursuit began on September 25 when officers attempted to stop a vehicle on Foxholes Road, which police said was linked to suspected drug dealing. Ishaq failed to stop and instead drove off, sparking the pursuit through Rochdale. His attempt to escape eventually came to an end when he crashed the vehicle. Police said Ishaq then tried to flee from officers on foot but was detained and arrested. He was subsequently charged with dangerous driving, driving while disqualified, failing to stop and driving without insurance.

candidates.source_title: Appeal over student accommodation at former care home is dismissed - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Planners' refusal of a bid to turn a former care home into university accommodation has been upheld.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: An appeal over plans to turn a former care home into university accommodation has been dismissed. The Al Sadiq Academy appealed to the Planning Inspectorate after Rochdale Council refused permission to change the use of the former Briarmede care home, in Rochdale Road, Middleton, into university accommodation. The plans included creating 11 en-suite bedrooms, with kitchens and dining hall/games room, library, study rooms, computer rooms and toilets on the ground floor. Planning offices recommended approval for the application, which would have included conditions the building is solely for the use of residents and was not used to provide classes, education services or private or community events at any time. But the application was called in by the council’s planning committee which refused it following concerns about the need for the facility, and the impact it would have on neighbours. In delivering the appeal decision, planning inspector K Mee said: “The main issues are whether the appeal site is a suitable location having regard to the local development plan, insofar as it relates to the type of accommodation; and the effect of the proposed development on the character of the surrounding area and the living conditions of neighbouring residents, with regard to noise and disturbance. “The appellant identifies a number of higher education institutions across Greater Manchester, including Hopwood Hall College opposite the appeal site, as potential sources of demand for student accommodation. “However, no substantive evidence has been provided to demonstrate that these institutions have been consulted regarding the proposals, nor that there is an identified unmet need for additional student accommodation either locally or across the wider area.

candidates.source_summary: A Heywood restaurant has won top honours at a national awards ceremony.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A Heywood restaurant has won top honours at a national awards ceremony. The Venus Lounge was crowned Restaurant of the Year at the National Curry Awards 2026, held yesterday at the House of Lords. The report said: “A small number of schools have seen too many empty seats over the last few years as intake numbers reduced and a low intake in 2027 is going to see additional financial pressures on those schools. “Current birth rates indicate a steady but slow rise in the years to 2030. The current projected intake for 2030 is approximately 2,900 and includes children from new housing developments across the borough.” In September, 2024, 90 surplus Reception places were removed, followed by an additional 35 for September, 2025. The report warns that further reductions are needed in some areas of the borough where there are too many empty places. While recent years have seen an average of 113 children needing places after moving into the borough each year, this figure has fallen to 20 over the past two years. As well as fewer children entering primary schools, there has been an average of 30 pupils per year not taking up secondary school places within the borough.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Port Vale boss Jon Brady was delighted his side finally found their shooting boots in their 4-2 win at home to Rochdale. Vale had only found the net six times in their previous 11 League Two games but, after Onel Hernandez put them ahead 90 seconds in, George Byers’ penalty and a third from Jordan Gabriel put them 3-0 up inside 22 minutes. Keyrol Figueroa scored Vale’s fourth late on, either side of the visitors’ goals, and Brady focused on a fine day for them. “First off we were very clinical in what we did,” he said. “We created loads of chances and the way we played, especially in that first half, was really pleasing. “To concede those two is disappointing but I want to focus on the positives. We’ve scored four goals at home, three from open play. Some of the delivery, some of our play was really positive today. “Onel stood out for me, he was excellent, his movement was great for the first goal and the way he finished it was brilliant. Then to get the penalty really made a difference after breaking through their back line and Gabby following up well after a great strike from Demo (Kyle Dempsey). At the end it’s great work from George Hall and Figgy knows where the back of the net is. “We’ve got to keep looking forward, we’ve been in tough situations, we said last week (defeat at York) had to be just a bump in the road and we’ve bounced back this week. I’m really pleased with the group, with everyone.” After his side shipped five against Accrington last week, Dale boss Ian Watson had watched in horror as they conceded three early goals.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Three early goals saw Port Vale ease to a 4-2 win at home to Rochdale in League Two. The Valiants had only hit six goals in 11 league games but with some dismal Dale defending they virtually sealed victory after 22 minutes. Onel Hernandez opened the scoring inside 90 seconds, gathering Kyle Dempsey’s through-ball and finding the bottom corner. Vale doubled their lead after 11 minutes. Aden Flint tripped Hernandez and George Byers fired the resulting penalty past Sam Waller. Dale threatened momentarily when Cian Hayes sent former Vale striker Dajaune Brown through, but he was thwarted by Jasper Moon. Moments later Vale scored their third. Dempsey’s shot was parried by Waller and Jordan Gabriel reacted first to slot home the rebound. With the game over as a contest, the second half produced few chances but ended with a flurry of goals. Dale’s Ian Henderson headed in after 82 minutes before Keyrol Figueroa restored Vale’s three-goal cushion with a simple tap-in four minutes from time.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Three early first-half goals plus a late fourth helped the Valiants to a relatively comfortable home victory over Rochdale. Note: Due to a holiday (and limited wifi) Rob's match report is minimal for this game. If you want to expand on the report please add your comments at the end Manager Jon Brady made four changes from the game against Manchester City including the return of attacking duo Onel Hernandez and Max Watters. The duo combined to give Vale an early goal. Watters headed down a ball to Dempsey and his delightful dinked pass found Hernandez who beat the keeper. It was 1-0 after just two minutes. The second arrived just nine minutes later. Aidan Flint clipped Hernandez in the box and captain George Byers made no mistake from the resulting penalty kick. It was 3-0 on 22 minutes when the Rochdale keeper kept out Dempsey's fierce drive but Gabriel was on hand to convert the loose ball. It could have been more - with Watters heading one delightful move over the bar - but at the break the Valiants were comfortably ahead. The second-half was a different affair. Vale swopped the front duo and Rochdale made a host of changes. It resulted in the visitors having much more of the ball and although they created chances they could not beat Marosi in the Vale goal until 82 minutes when veteran Ian Henderson found the target. That was a blot on Vale's copybook but the Valiants countered with another goal for loanee Keyrol Figueroa. He latched on to a good cross from the impressive George Hall to restore Vale's three goal advantage. In the closing moments, Rochdale added a second. Marosi produced a great save from a header but the rebound was put away by Tasker. However, it was too little, too late. The first-half display was good while the second 45 minutes may not have been great at times. So, it was a game of two halves but this was still a decent victory for Vale and one which eases the pressure on manager Jon Brady. Full-time: Port Vale 4-2 Rochdale

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Empty and neglected buildings across the borough could be brought back into use with help from £2.24 million from the Government’s new Derelict Buildings Fund. Rochdale Council’s allocation, confirmed alongside Wednesday’s Budget, is part of a £125 million national fund to help councils transform derelict buildings into spaces their communities need. The money can be used to buy derelict buildings, close the viability gaps that stop regeneration schemes going ahead, and help community groups and local businesses take buildings over. Rochdale MP Paul Waugh will act as a Programme Champion for the fund. Government guidance will make clear that councils should work alongside local MPs when deciding which buildings and projects to back. The announcement comes as communities across the borough fight to save their locals. In Littleborough, there is strong interest in reopening The Wheatsheaf, part of the Grade II listed Roundhouse building dating from the early 1860s, which closed in June. Earlier this month, Rochdale Council passed a motion brought by Littleborough Lakeside Councillor Richard Jackson calling on the Government to block restrictive covenants on pub sales. Mr Waugh has supported this campaign directly having written to ministers urging action. These covenants allow pub companies selling a building to ban it from ever being used as a pub again, a restriction that binds every future owner. At his heaviest weight, Steven felt his health and lifestyle were preventing him from fully enjoying family life. The turning point came after seeing his wife achieve her own remarkable health transformation and realising, during a family holiday, how much his weight was limiting the experiences he could share with his children. Determined to make a change, Steven committed to taking control of his health and wellbeing. Although already a member of Heywood Sports Village, Steven admits he lacked the knowledge and confidence to train effectively. Working alongside Personal Trainer Alex, gave him the skills, guidance and accountability needed to achieve lasting results. Through structured training, nutritional support and regular encouragement, Steven gradually transformed both his body and mindset. Like any significant journey, there were challenges along the way. Today, Steven has lost an incredible 15 stone , completely transforming his quality of life. He now feels fitter, stronger and more confident than ever before. Activities that once seemed impossible, from everyday movement to family holidays, are now enjoyed with ease. Beyond the physical transformation, Steven says the greatest change has been the confidence gained from setting a challenging goal and proving to himself that he could achieve it. The new Rochdale fitness facility will become Mayfield’s main shirt sponsor for the 2027 and 2028 seasons, with its branding appearing on playing shirts from the youngest age groups through to the senior sides. The agreement takes the club into its 70th anniversary year in 2028. Mayfield said its playing kit programme for both seasons is now fully sponsored. Alongside the shirt sponsorship, Gymbound will provide access to its facilities for the club’s Open Age pre-season training programme ahead of the 2027 rugby league campaign. Players and club members will also be offered exclusive membership opportunities, while the two organisations plan to work together on future health, fitness and community initiatives. Carl Abraham, speaking on behalf of Rochdale Mayfield, said the training and membership arrangements were an important part of the agreement. “What makes this partnership particularly exciting is that it goes far beyond simply having a company’s name on our playing shirts. The support Gymbound will provide through our Open Age pre-season programme, alongside exclusive membership opportunities for our players and members, demonstrates a genuine commitment to investing in the health, fitness and wellbeing of our club.” Mayfield was established in 1958 and now has 17 teams. The club says its activities involve participants from three years old through to people in their seventies, with Women’s Masters, Disability Rugby League and community wellbeing programmes alongside its other rugby league teams.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Find out the latest events from October 31 from All Across the Arts columnist Steve Cooke A great opportunity to share ideas on how we can transform parks, public spaces and libraries into cultural and creative hubs for our communities. Building on conversations regarding ‘Third Spaces’ and ‘Everyday Utopias’ held with Kitty’s Launderette at a previous Lab Session, they are inviting partners and local residents to share ideas on how new strategies led by the council’s parks, libraries and culture teams might help enhance these spaces as free to access cultural and community spaces. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A Greater Manchester Police officer who worked in Tameside has been dismissed after sharing confidential police information while in a relationship with a member of an organised crime group in Rochdale. Tubah Hamid was dismissed with immediate effect following an accelerated misconduct hearing held by GMP Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson. The hearing found breaches of the standards of professional behaviour relating to Honesty and Integrity, Discreditable Conduct, Confidentiality, and Orders and Instructions were proven and amounted to gross misconduct. In his decision, Sir Stephen said Hamid's culpability was 'very high', describing her actions as 'deliberate, persistent' and carried out in the 'full knowledge' that they were 'unlawful and morally indefensible'. He said the former constable had abused her position of responsibility, with her misconduct involving multiple incidents over a lengthy period and deliberate breaches of policies governing information held on police systems. Sir Stephen added that Hamid's unlawful accessing of police data demonstrated a 'distinct lack of integrity and moral fibre' and said she was 'manifestly unsuited to the office of constable'. Hamid was dismissed with immediate effect, and her name was ordered to be added to the College of Policing's Barred List. The disciplinary proceedings followed a criminal investigation into Hamid's conduct.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: As a new trial offering better mental health and social care support is launched in Rochdale, Minister of State for Public Health and Patient Safety Dame Diana Johnson tells the Rochdale Times how it will help young people and their families across the borough. “How many of us could have benefited from the understanding and guidance of a mental health professional while we were growing up? Growing up can be challenging for any child. Professor Peter Fonagy’s recent independent review of mental health conditions, ADHD and autism has highlighted the scale of the challenge. Mental health distress is rising, particularly among children and young people, with girls especially affected. Greater Manchester is not immune to this disturbing trend. For children already facing difficult circumstances, the health risks can be even greater. Children in contact with social services often have high levels of mental health need, alongside other challenges affecting their lives and wellbeing. That’s why I’m delighted Greater Manchester will lead the way in improving early mental health support for children through Care Together, a pilot designed to give children involved with social care services faster access to help. Backed by £6.4 million over three years, the programme will operate through NHS Pennine Trust, working with councils in Stockport, Tameside and Rochdale.

candidates.source_title: New trial gives children better mental health and social care support - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Children and young people supported by social care in Rochdale will benefit from faster, simpler access to mental health and care support under a new Government pilot.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Children and young people supported by social care in Rochdale will benefit from faster, simpler access to mental health and care support under a new Government pilot. Care Together will test and evaluate a new model of care, embedding mental health professionals from existing NHS services into children’s social care settings. The pilot aims to replace fragmented provision with faster access to expert, needs-led mental health support, including family therapy and support for parents and primary caregivers. The Government is investing up to £9.4 million over three years in the Care Together pilot, which will be run by Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board (ICB), working with Stockport, Tameside, and Rochdale local authorities. The pilot follows Professor Peter Fonagy’s independent review into mental health conditions, ADHD and autism, which recommended better integrated mental health support. The latest figures on children in need, children on protection plans, children in care, and care leavers, including adopted children, across the three participating local authority areas show up to 7,000 children and young people, as well as their parents, carers, and/or guardians, will be covered by the pilot. By bringing social care and mental health professionals together in one team, children, young people, and their families will have faster access to support tailored to their needs, reducing the need to navigate multiple services. Dame Diana Johnson, Minister of State for Public Health and Patient Safety, said: “For too long, fragmented mental health services have left young people in care, care leavers, parents, carers, and guardians not knowing where to turn for support.
